Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

EarthFlux 0.1.0.9000 (development version)

New features

  • Automatic search and download of the MODIS granules of the surface state (internal, for the coming earthflux()): the sinusoidal tiles under an area of interest, one NASA CMR granule per product, tile and date (MOD11A1/MYD11A1, MCD43A3, MOD13A2, MCD15A2H; composite periods from the granule metadata), and the LP DAAC download with the NASA Earthdata token read only from EARTHDATA_TOKEN, into a validated cache (tools::R_user_dir("EarthFlux", "cache") by default). Areas that need more than one tile are not assembled yet.

  • Automatic elevation model (internal, for the coming earthflux(); decision M5-06): NASADEM_HGT v001 tiles are found with NASA CMR, downloaded from LP DAAC with the Earthdata token of the environment, validated and cached, and turned into elevation, slope, aspect, mean normal length and valid fraction on the 1 km working grid, either flat or with the CANDIDATA mean-normal chain (3 arc-second slopes averaged as unit normal vectors). Water and missing tiles are never filled.

  • Station-free weather forcing (decision M5-07, internal for now): hourly ERA5 data from the Open-Meteo historical weather API (models=era5) for the ERA5 cells covering an area of interest plus a one-cell buffer, each cell a virtual station of ef_station_table() (wind at 10 m, elevation from the API, UTC), so that QC, reference ET and regionalization work unchanged. Explicit choices without defaults for the elevation adjustment and the treatment of the instantaneous values; optional apikey for the customer (commercial) API, never stored; JSON cache; CC BY 4.0 and Copernicus attribution in the provenance. New flag EF_WS_GRIDDED_FORCING (warning, object scope). Adds jsonlite to Imports.

  • earthflux(aoi, date, weather, preset), the integrated workflow (decisions M5-04 and M5-08 to M5-22): MODIS surface state and NASADEM elevation downloaded and prepared on the 1 km MODIS grid, weather from a station table (one station: its values everywhere; several: inverse distance weighting) or from ERA5 via Open-Meteo, hourly alfalfa reference ET and wind regionalized and interpolated to the overpass time of each cell, anchors selected before the net radiation (incoming longwave from the cold anchor), calibration of dT and daily ETa. Returns an earthflux_result with every intermediate layer, the objects of each stage, flag words per stage, flags and a provenance with every effective option (print(), summary() and plot() methods). Two presets, idaho2002_elev and idaho2002_flat (SEBAL Idaho manual forms with and without its elevation adjustments, both CANDIDATA, version 1), listed by ef_presets() and shown in full by ef_preset(); a preset that is not verified raises one earthflux_unverified_preset_warning listing its unverified elements. New flag EF_H_ZOM_UNDEFINED (info, cell scope, bit 10 of the H word): the momentum roughness length is 0 where LAI is 0 and no minimum is applied, so the cell is NA from the sensible heat flux on. New error class earthflux_weather_coverage_error.

  • Presets idaho2002_elev and idaho2002_flat version 2 (decisions M5-23 and M5-24; the changes are listed in ef_preset(name)$changes and in the provenance). Anchor criteria recalibrated for 1 km MODIS pixels on the Cauquenes and Maule scenes of 2019-02-15: cold candidates with NDVI at or above the 90th percentile and white-sky albedo in [0.14, 0.26], hot candidates with NDVI at or below the 10th percentile and albedo in [0.18, 0.35] (no absolute LAI thresholds), one relaxation step (percentiles 0.80 and 0.20), and no anchor on cells whose LAI was assigned by lai_nonveg; still CANDIDATA. The momentum roughness length now has a minimum of 0.005 m (CANDIDATA) where 0.018 LAI is below it, flagged with the new EF_H_ZOM_FLOOR_APPLIED (info, cell scope, bit 1 of the H word), so cells with LAI = 0 get an ETa. EF_H_ZOM_UNDEFINED is retired (no function raises it any more); its bit 10 stays reserved and the registry refuses retired codes and bits.

Changes

  • ef_h_control() has one convergence control per phase of ef_calibrate_h() (decision M2-11): tol and maxit now apply to the calibration at the anchors only, with defaults 1e-6 and 100 (were 0.01 and 20), and the new pixel_tol (default 1e-5) and pixel_maxit (default 100) to the per-pixel stability iteration. With the former shared 1 % tolerance the anchors stopped short of their fixed point, so the anchors run through the pixel phase no longer reproduced their target H and every pixel inherited the offset: in a strongly unstable, low-wind Landsat scene (the Talca example of the water package) H was 0.59 W m-2 below the fixed point on average (up to 1.3 W m-2); with the new defaults it is within 5e-4 W m-2, at about 1.5 times the run time. Pixels that do not converge keep their flag EF_H_PIXEL_NOT_CONVERGED and now also raise one earthflux_convergence_warning (field phase = "pixels"). The former behaviour is ef_h_control(tol = 0.01, maxit = 20, pixel_tol = 0.01, pixel_maxit = 20).

  • Presets idaho2002_elev and idaho2002_flat version 3: the convergence settings of the calibration of H are written out in the preset (tol = 1e-6, maxit = 100, pixel_tol = 1e-5, pixel_maxit = 100; decision M2-11) and recorded in the provenance with every other option. H changes by up to about 1.3 W m-2.

  • Presets idaho2002_elev and idaho2002_flat version 4: a terrain rule (decision M5-25, CANDIDATA). One linear dT calibrated between two anchors with one weather forcing only holds over the elevations of the calibration, so cells more than the limit of the preset below or above the elevation range of the calibration hold no anchor and are NA in every layer of the result. The range spans the cold and hot anchors of a preliminary anchor selection without the rule and, with one station, the station (the datum of the surface temperature and the site of the forcing); cells between the anchors are kept, however far from each. The limits differ per preset: 500 m for idaho2002_elev, whose lapse correction leaves an error of about 3.3 K per km in the datum surface temperature, and 250 m for idaho2002_flat, which has no lapse correction (6.5 K per km); both keep that error within the 1.5 K homogeneity tolerance of the anchors. They are flagged with the new EF_H_TERRAIN_RULE_APPLIED (info, cell scope, bit 11 of the H word; the other words are NA there) and counted in the provenance (terrain_rule_excluded, below and above the range, with the reference elevations, the kept range and the final anchors in scene$terrain_rule). On the Maule scene of 2019-02-15 the elev preset loses the Andes above about 800 m (40 % of the computed cells), where ETrF was mostly negative, and keeps the hot anchor in valley fields; the flat preset loses 46 %. On the Cauquenes scene the elev preset is unchanged and the flat preset loses 18 cells above 669 m. The excluded cells get no ETa.

Bug fixes

  • The MODIS readers and modis_provenance() now work with older and newer terra alike. terra::metags() returns a named character vector up to terra 1.8-29 and a data frame (with metadata domains) from 1.8-42, and terra::gdal(lib = "all") returns a named character vector up to 1.9-45 and a data frame from 1.9-46; both shapes are now handled. With terra 1.7-65 the tag lookup failed (“missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”) and the provenance record failed on $.

  • DESCRIPTION now requires terra (>= 1.7-65), the oldest release on which the test suite has been run (metags() itself exists from 1.7-55). A new CI job (min-terra) runs R CMD check with R 4.3 and that terra release, so regressions on the minimum are caught.

Documentation

  • ef_station_ref_et(): the daily sum of the hourly reference ET is the daily reference ET of the METRIC extrapolation verified against the SEBAL Idaho manual (Waters et al., 2002, Eq. 44); the documentation said it was still to be checked.

  • citation("EarthFlux") and CITATION.cff give the Zenodo DOI of the package (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23981325, which resolves to the latest release; 0.1.0 is 10.5281/zenodo.23981326), and the README shows how to cite it.

  • The maps of the README and of the Example scene: Cauquenes article are shown in geographic coordinates (EPSG:4326); the computations stay on the native MODIS grid.

  • New website article Hot and cold anchors and the Monin–Obukhov iteration: why the sensible heat flux is calibrated with anchor pixels, how dT = a + b Ts_datum is solved, and the stability iteration of ef_calibrate_h() written out step by step on the cauquenes_modis scene (with an illustrative weather station and elevation), checked against the function and with convergence, neutral versus stability corrected H and per-cell iteration figures.

  • Spanish version of that article for university teaching, Píxeles ancla y la iteración de Monin–Obukhov, with the same code, data and verification and the figure labels in Spanish; the two versions link to each other.

EarthFlux 0.1.0

First release of EarthFlux. It is experimental and not for operational or scientific production use: no result has been validated yet, and interfaces may change. The integrated earthflux() workflow, its presets, the automatic download of MODIS products, elevation models and weather forcing, and validation results are not part of this release.

Verification

  • Reference evapotranspiration (FAO-56, worked examples 18 and 19 reproduced; ASCE-EWRI 2005), unit conversions and MODIS product facts are VERIFICADA against their primary sources.
  • Most METRIC formulations are VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002): checked, with page and equation, against the SEBAL Idaho manual of the METRIC authors (Waters et al., 2002); the Perrier roughness against Allen et al. (2012, IAHS Publ. 352). The cross-check with Allen, Tasumi & Trezza (2007) remains desirable.
  • The stable momentum correction at the blending height is psi_m(200 m) = -5 (2 / L) (Eq. 38), so ef_h_control() defaults stable_psi_m_height to 2 m; the verified heights (200, 0.1 and 2 m) and c_p = 1004 J kg-1 K-1 are defaults too. The Monin-Obukhov length uses the surface temperature and g = 9.81 m s-2 (Eq. 34).
  • Still CANDIDATA, as explicit arguments without defaults: the partitioned shortwave transmissivity, the terrain projection of the incoming shortwave radiation, the incidence angle on a tilted plane, G of Tasumi, the FAO-56 air density in METRIC, the anchor selection criteria and ef_lambda(method = "metric"). Open: the temperature of the incoming longwave radiation (ef_rl_in()) and the emissivity of non-vegetated pixels (lai_nonveg). The register is dev/VERIFICATION.md in the source repository.

New features

  • METRIC core. The chain as numeric functions, from solar geometry to daily actual ET: radiation components and ef_net_radiation(), soil heat flux (ef_g()), anchor pixels (ef_select_anchors(), ef_anchors(), ef_anchor_conditions()), roughness, wind, friction velocity and aerodynamic resistance (ef_zom(), ef_ustar(), ef_rah()), the dT calibration and sensible heat (ef_calibrate_h(), ef_sensible_heat()), latent heat and ET (ef_latent_heat(), ef_et_inst(), ef_etrf(), ef_et_daily()).
  • Method families. Each family has a dispatcher with an explicit method and no default (e.g. ef_g(method = "bastiaanssen")), returning a classed object with the value, the method, diagnostic flags and provenance; the method functions return plain numerics.
  • Meteorological forcing. Weather station tables (ef_station_table()) with quality control (ef_station_qc()), derived variables verified against FAO-56 (vapour pressure, dew point, psychrometric constant, wind at 2 m, extraterrestrial and clear-sky radiation) and reference ET at the stations (ef_ref_et(), ef_station_ref_et()).
  • Spatial regionalization. ef_regionalize() maps a station variable onto the working grid by a representative station, global regression, inverse distance weighting or geographically weighted regression on an internal GWR core (ef_gwr_fit(), ef_gwr_predict()), with exact block prediction, spatial block cross-validation (ef_spatial_folds(), ef_regionalize_cv()) and optional parallel execution under a future plan.
  • MODIS surface state (internal, not exported yet): reading of local MODIS files, scaling, QA bits as flags, view time to UTC, broadband albedo and emissivity, temporal matching and aggregation to the native 1 km grid of the land surface temperature.
  • Example data. cauquenes_modis: the MODIS surface state of the Cauquenes province (Maule Region, Chile) on 15 February 2019.

Changes

  • Results are flagged, never silently corrected: one registry of diagnostic flags per stage (69 codes), classed conditions for errors and warnings.
  • Physical constants are defined once, with unit, source and verification status.
  • End-to-end tests run synthetic scenes through the METRIC chain, the forcing and the MODIS surface state.
  • EarthFlux imports terra, future, future.apply and stats; GWmodel is suggested for the cross-verification of the GWR core.

Documentation

  • README with the status of the release and an example on cauquenes_modis; introductory vignette; website articles Design and development status and Example scene: Cauquenes.
  • pkgdown site at https://djwillichile.github.io/EarthFlux/.
  • Continuous integration on Linux, Windows and macOS; GitHub releases built from the version tag; Zenodo archive of each release.
